---
title: 3 - Map view
---

Now that your webmap includes the desired WMS layer, you will adjust the map so that Tanzania is visible when the application opens.

In this chapter, you will learn how to:

- Set the initial centre and zoom level of the map.
- Control the size and position of the map on the web page.
- Separate the page structure in HTML from the styling in CSS.


## 3.1. Set the initial map view

Open `main.js` and locate the map configuration, beginning with `const map = new Map({`.

Inside this configuration, find the `view` property. The OpenLayers `View` determines the initial centre, zoom level and projection of the map.

### Edit the map centre and zoom

Replace the existing centre and zoom values with the values provided below. The `centre` coordinates represent a point approximately at the center of Tanzania, and the slightly increased `zoom` parameter brings the default map view a bit closer.

```javascript
const map = new Map({
  layers: layers,
  target: 'map',
  view: new View({
    center: [3862074, -732904],
    zoom: 6,
  }),
});
```

Save `main.js` and refresh the webmap. The map should now open over Tanzania, with the *Tanzania World Heritage and Ramsar Sites 2026* layer visible. 

*Screenshot 1: Tanzania visible in the map after adjusting the initial view.*


## 3.2. Adjust the map window

The map's initial centre and zoom control what you see, but they do not determine how much screen space the map occupies.

Open `style.css`. We will use CSS to make the map fill the browser window, instead of just half of it. Add the following code that defines the map window to be full screen. There is nothing much in the style.css file yet, so add this block just at the end of the existing code. 

``` css
#map {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  right: 0;
}
```

Save the `style.css` file and refresh the map. You should now see a full-window map rather than a map restricted to a smaller area of the page.

*Screenshot 2: The full-window map after updating the CSS.*


## 3.3. Keep the HTML and CSS organised

Open `index.html` and inspect the document's `<head>` section.

!You may find that the map's appearance has been defined directly inside a `<style>` element. This works, but as the webmap becomes more complex, it is easier to manage the appearance in a separate stylesheet.!

Remove the existing inline map styling and add a link to `style.css` inside the `<head>` element:

!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <title>Tanzania forest reserves and conservation areas</title>

    <!-- This is custom stylesheet that refers to our style.css file -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
  </head>


The browser will now load the map's styling from `style.css`. This keeps the HTML responsible for the page structure and the CSS responsible for its appearance.

You can also change the HTML `<title>` to a meaningful name for your webmap. For example:

`Tanzania forest reserves and conservation areas`

This text appears in the browser tab; it is separate from a title displayed inside the map itself.

Save the file and refresh the application.


### Checkpoint

Your webmap should now:

- Open with Tanzania in view.
- Fill the available browser window.
- Load its styles from `style.css`.
- Display the correct project title in the browser tab.

*Screenshot 3: The completed map view, with Tanzania visible and the map filling the browser window.*

### Further reading

- [OpenLayers Basic Concepts](https://openlayers.org/doc/tutorials/concepts.html)
- [OpenLayers Quick Start](https://openlayers.org/doc/quickstart.html)







Edit the map window size and its default view.

We want the map to pan to Tanzania directly when it loads. Scroll down in main.js to section where the map itself is configured (const map = new Map({). Here, edit the center and zoom of the map view. Center should be coordinates of the center point of the map that loads when opened. We can use approximately the center point of Tanzania. Zoom was initially 8, but change it to 6 as tanzania is a bit smaller coutnry than the US, and we would like the map to be zoomed in a bit more. Save.

```javascript
const map = new Map({
  layers: layers,
  target: 'map',
  view: new View({
    center: [3862074, -732904],
    zoom: 6,
  }),
});
```
Here, the
- `center` is changed to coordinates of a point in the middle of Tanzania
- `zoom` is changed slightly larger to get a closer view of Tanzania

Once at it, edit the map window, too. Go to style.css file and add the following code that defines the map window to be full screen (instead of just a half-page). There is nothing much in the style.css file, and add this block just at the end of the existing code. 

#map {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  right: 0;
}

Open index.html. There you see a similar block of code inside the <style> section. Indeed, we CAN define the map window here as well, but for elegancy, we'll use styles.css for any styling elements and just refer to them in the index.html. This is to prevent the index.html expanding too much. 

Delete the code inside <style> and instead, add a reference to the style.css code like this:

!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <title>Tanzania forest reserves and conservation areas</title>

    <!-- This is custom stylesheet that refers to our style.css file -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
  </head>

As you can see, here you can also change the title of your webmap project. Change the Simgle image WMS to "Tanzania forest reserves and conservation areas". This title will be visible in the browser tab when you open the webmap.
